metaTitle: Mercedes Engine Bearing Replacement | Mercedes Garage
metaDescription: Professional engine bearing replacement for Mercedes-Benz models. We replace main bearings and connecting rod bearings with OEM-spec parts. Get a quote today.
lede: Expert bottom-end bearing replacement for Mercedes petrol and diesel engines. Performed as part of a full engine rebuild with OEM-spec parts and precision assembly.

blocks.html: Engine bearing replacement is a bottom-end rebuild operation. We remove the engine from the vehicle, mount it on a stand, and carry out the following steps:

items: **Access & Disassembly** - Drain fluids, remove all external components (manifolds, turbochargers, accessories), and strip the engine to access the crankshaft.
**Crankshaft Removal** - Remove the oil pan and crankshaft to expose the main bearing shells and connecting rod bearings.
**Bearing Replacement** - Fit new OEM-spec main and connecting rod bearing shells, using colour-coded matching to the crankshaft and block. Replace thrust washers where fitted.
**Clearance Measurement** - Verify bearing clearances with Plastigage or dial bore gauges to ensure they meet factory specifications.
**Reassembly** - Install new torque-to-yield bolts, follow precise torque sequences and angles, and replace all gaskets and seals.
**Testing** - Run the engine on a test stand or in-vehicle to verify oil pressure, temperature, and overall performance before handover.

blocks.html: We use genuine Mercedes parts and OE-spec consumables throughout. Every rebuild includes a full inspection of all bottom-end components.

items.q: Is engine bearing replacement always part of a full rebuild?
items.a: Yes. Bearings cannot be replaced in isolation on Mercedes engines without fully stripping the bottom end. We always perform a complete rebuild, replacing bearings, seals, gaskets, and any other worn components.

items.q: How do you ensure the correct bearing clearances?
items.a: We measure crankshaft journals with precision micrometers and dial bore gauges. We then select the correct colour-coded bearing shells from the Mercedes-supplied set and verify clearance with Plastigage.

items.q: Do you reuse the old bolts?
items.a: Never. All main bearing cap and connecting rod bolts are torque-to-yield and must be replaced with new ones. We use genuine Mercedes bolts every time.

items.q: How long does the work take?
items.a: Typically, the engine is removed, rebuilt, and refitted within 3-5 working days, depending on the model and any additional work required.
